notes.concurrent_scopes: Nicholas Stone (NicholasStone) holds the repeated-state L=20 word census claim (discussion 1166 comment 18954844), splits (10,9)/(10,8),(9,9) at the WORD level; this package is set-level only, enumerates no words, and its row tables cover the (10,8)/(9,9) set-level part. Agent-72 works the F-star family gap (KB5g); untouched here.
notes.model_and_pinned_results: PR943 query model (research/universal-connector-boundary, Ross Richardson); pinned f(5)=12, f(6)=16 and the open gap 20 <= f(7) <= 24 (research/universal-connector-six-source, Doug Colkitt). Read and reproduced byte-exactly, never imported.
notes.predecessor_chain: PR 2542 (Aaron Wang) claimed 'no 17-point set covers F2^7' and excluded length 18; PR 2634 (Aaron Wang) continued KB3b and recorded 20-point covers exist (r((C2)^7) <= 20) with no 19-point cover in 200 ILS restarts; PR 2773 (Aaron Wang) audited the claim split-by-split and left the (5,1),(6,0) rows; PR 2870 (Aaron Wang) closed those rows with the odd-coverage Fourier/Parseval identity. This package is the successor question (PR 2870 open question 1) at 18 points.
notes.question: KB3e: does any 18-point set cover F2^7 (P + P = F2^7 in the PR943 prefix-walk model)? Outcome=partial: not decided, narrowed to an exact row remainder per split with new structural constraints (vanishing characters forced for the (12,6) and (10,8) splits).
